Package io.telekom.orchest.adapter.mongo.scheduler

Class MongoScheduledTaskStore

java.lang.Object
io.telekom.orchest.adapter.mongo.scheduler.MongoScheduledTaskStore
All Implemented Interfaces:
io.telekom.orchest.scheduling.spi.ScheduledTaskStore
@Repository public class MongoScheduledTaskStore extends Object implements io.telekom.orchest.scheduling.spi.ScheduledTaskStore
MongoDB-backed reference implementation of ScheduledTaskStore.

Atomicity strategy — every mutating operation lands as a single findAndModify on the scheduledTasks collection, which Mongo guarantees to be atomic on a single document. That is sufficient for distributed safety because the entire task row is one document. We deliberately avoid multi-document transactions so the store also works on standalone Mongo deployments (only a replica set was previously required because of the TTL + change-stream design).

Claim semantics — claimDue(String, Instant, Duration, int) loops batchSize times, each iteration calling findAndModify with the predicate (state == PENDING AND triggerAt <= now) OR (state == RUNNING AND leaseUntil < now), sorted by triggerAt ASC. Because each iteration is its own atomic operation, two dispatchers polling concurrently will simply walk past each other — the loser sees the row already flipped to RUNNING with a fresh lease and skips it.

Optimistic concurrency — completeAndDelete(String, long), fail(String, long, Instant, String) and markDead(String, long, String) each include version == expected in their query. If the lease was stolen by another dispatcher (because the original worker stalled past leaseUntil), the version will have advanced and the operation becomes a no-op — matching the SPI contract.
